titulo: Quiz — The Spanish clock and the bar dossier
subtitulo: Twenty past seven, a neighbourhood bar, and everything from episode one arriving at once
introPt: Quiz time. It's twenty past seven in the evening, somewhere in Madrid, and our two travellers walk into a proper neighbourhood bar — no photographs on the menu, which is already a good sign. In the next ninety seconds they get the kitchen hours, the three prices, the truth about the free tapa and a booking for later. Listen as many times as you like, then answer.
cenario: A traveller walks into a neighbourhood bar at 19:20, finds the kitchen closed, orders a beer at the bar instead, checks the prices and the tapa, books a table for half nine and pays.

dialogo.pt: — Good afternoon. (said on the way IN)

dialogo.es: Ahora solo bebidas. La cocina abre a las ocho y media.
dialogo.pinyin: ah-OH-rah SOH-loh beh-BEE-dhahs. lah koh-THEE-nah AH-breh ah lahs OH-choh ee MEH-dhyah
dialogo.pt: — Just drinks for now. The kitchen opens at half past eight.

dialogo.es: Vale. Pues ponme una caña, por favor.
dialogo.pinyin: BAH-leh. pwehs POHN-meh OO-nah KAH-nyah, por fah-BOR
dialogo.pt: — Fair enough. A small draught beer then, please.

dialogo.es: ¿Es el mismo precio en la barra?
dialogo.pinyin: es el MEES-moh PREH-thyoh en lah BAH-rrah
dialogo.pt: — Is it the same price at the bar?

dialogo.es: En la barra es más barato. En la terraza hay suplemento.
dialogo.pinyin: en lah BAH-rrah es mahs bah-RAH-toh. en lah teh-RRAH-thah ai soo-pleh-MEN-toh
dialogo.pt: — At the bar it's cheaper. On the terrace there's a surcharge.

dialogo.es: ¿Y la tapa va incluida con la bebida?
dialogo.pinyin: ee lah TAH-pah bah een-kloo-EE-dhah kon lah beh-BEE-dhah
dialogo.pt: — And does the tapa come with the drink?

dialogo.es: Aquí no, cariño. Esto no es Granada.
dialogo.pinyin: ah-KEE noh, kah-REE-nyoh. EHS-toh noh es grah-NAH-dhah
dialogo.pt: — Not here, love. This isn't Granada.

dialogo.es: Entendido. Quiero reservar una mesa para las nueve y media.
dialogo.pinyin: en-ten-DEE-dhoh. KYEH-roh rreh-sehr-BAR OO-nah MEH-sah PAH-rah lahs NWEH-beh ee MEH-dhyah
dialogo.pt: — Understood. I'd like to book a table for half past nine.
— Perfect. How many of you are there? (👂 that's vosotros — you'll hear it constantly and never need to say it)

dialogo.pinyin: SOH-mohs dohs. nohs KOH-brahs, por fah-BOR
dialogo.pt: — Two of us. Can we pay, please?

perguntas.es: It's twenty past seven. What does she tell him about food?
perguntas.pergunta: It's twenty past seven. What does she tell him about food?
opcoes: Drinks only for now — the kitchen opens at half past eight
The kitchen is closed for the rest of the night
They're fully booked until half past eight
They only serve food on the terrace
perguntas.pt: 'Ahora solo bebidas. La cocina abre a las ocho y media.' — the standard answer before eight. The bar is open; the kitchen simply hasn't started. Not a rejection: a timetable.
perguntas.explica: 'Ahora solo bebidas. La cocina abre a las ocho y media.' — the standard answer before eight. The bar is open; the kitchen simply hasn't started. Not a rejection: a timetable.

perguntas.es: The barwoman's first word to him is 'Dime'. What is she doing?
perguntas.pergunta: The barwoman's first word to him is 'Dime'. What is she doing?
opcoes: Telling him to wait his turn
Asking him to repeat himself
Telling him it's his turn — go ahead and order
Asking whether he has a reservation
perguntas.pt: 'Dime' — literally 'tell me'. It's an invitation, not impatience. Look up, answer it, and order in one short sentence. Look at the floor instead and you'll still be standing there in twenty minutes.
perguntas.explica: 'Dime' — literally 'tell me'. It's an invitation, not impatience. Look up, answer it, and order in one short sentence. Look at the floor instead and you'll still be standing there in twenty minutes.

perguntas.es: He asks '¿Es el mismo precio en la barra?'. What does she tell him?
perguntas.pergunta: He asks '¿Es el mismo precio en la barra?'. What does she tell him?
opcoes: Everything costs the same wherever you sit
The bar is cheaper; the terrace carries a surcharge
The terrace is cheaper before eight
There's a minimum spend on the terrace
perguntas.pt: Three prices for one beer — barra, mesa, terraza — and it's perfectly legal, as long as it's on the displayed price list. Asking before you sit down is the whole trick.
perguntas.explica: Three prices for one beer — barra, mesa, terraza — and it's perfectly legal, as long as it's on the displayed price list. Asking before you sit down is the whole trick.

perguntas.es: Does the tapa come free with the beer in this bar?
perguntas.pergunta: Does the tapa come free with the beer in this bar?
opcoes: Yes — free tapas are the law across Spain
Yes, but only with the first drink
No — free tapas are a regional habit, not a Spanish law
No, because he ordered at the bar rather than at a table
perguntas.pt: 'Esto no es Granada.' Free tapas is a Granada habit — plus eastern Andalusia and pockets of León and Galicia. In Madrid, Barcelona, San Sebastián and Valencia, the tapa is a paid item. Ask, don't assume.
perguntas.explica: 'Esto no es Granada.' Free tapas is a Granada habit — plus eastern Andalusia and pockets of León and Galicia. In Madrid, Barcelona, San Sebastián and Valencia, the tapa is a paid item. Ask, don't assume.

perguntas.es: What time does he book the table for?
perguntas.pergunta: What time does he book the table for?
opcoes: Eight o'clock
Half past eight
Nine o'clock
Half past nine
perguntas.pt: 'Para las nueve y media' — half nine, a completely normal Spanish dinner booking. He didn't storm off at half seven; he came back at the hour the country actually eats.
perguntas.explica: 'Para las nueve y media' — half nine, a completely normal Spanish dinner booking. He didn't storm off at half seven; he came back at the hour the country actually eats.

perguntas.es: She asks '¿Cuántos sois?'. What does she want to know?
perguntas.pergunta: She asks '¿Cuántos sois?'. What does she want to know?
opcoes: How many of you there are
What time you'd like the table
Whether you've booked before
How long you're staying in the city
perguntas.pt: That's vosotros — the plural 'you' that only exists in Spain, and the reason this form catches people out. You'll be on the receiving end of it fifty times a day and you'll almost never need to produce it. Recognise it, answer 'somos dos', move on.
perguntas.explica: That's vosotros — the plural 'you' that only exists in Spain, and the reason this form catches people out. You'll be on the receiving end of it fifty times a day and you'll almost never need to produce it. Recognise it, answer 'somos dos', move on.

perguntas.es: 'Son tres euros con cincuenta.' How much is the beer?
perguntas.pergunta: 'Son tres euros con cincuenta.' How much is the beer?
perguntas.pt: Cincuenta is 50 — 'theen-KWEN-tah', with the 'th' of 'think' at the front. Sesenta is 60, and starts with a plain 's'. That one sound is the difference between the two numbers you'll hear most often at a till, so train the ear: the 'th' means fifty.
